name: Molybdenum
mobility: Moderately mobile (symptoms on OLDER-to-MIDDLE leaves + young distortion; N-deficiency-like in legumes)

overview.whyImportant: Molybdenum is needed in the tiniest amounts but is essential for two key enzymes: nitrate reductase (converts nitrate to usable N) and nitrogenase (biological N-fixation in legume nodules). Deficiency is worst on ACID soils and shows as N-deficiency-like yellowing plus the classic cauliflower 'whiptail'.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Cofactor of nitrate reductase and nitrogenase enzymes.
plantFunctions.proteinSynthesis: Essential — without Mo, nitrate can't be reduced to build proteins.
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Critical for legume N-fixation and nitrate-fed crops; large effect in pulses and crucifers.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Molybdate availability DROPS in acid soils (opposite of most micronutrients); liming cures it.
Leaching and acidification of light soils.
High sulphate competes with molybdate uptake.
Poor nodulation compounds N problems in legumes.
Not liming acid soils; ignoring Mo seed treatment in legumes/crucifers.

symptoms.note: Because Mo runs N metabolism, deficiency LOOKS like nitrogen deficiency (pale older-mid leaves) PLUS young-leaf distortion; classic 'whiptail' in cauliflower.
symptoms.middle: Interveinal/marginal chlorosis, upward cupping, marginal scorching; poor nodulation in legumes.
symptoms.severe: Cauliflower WHIPTAIL — leaf blades fail to expand, become thin strap/whip-like; no curd; legumes N-starved despite N present.
symptoms.youngLeaves: Distorted, cupped, strap-like (whiptail) in severe cases.
symptoms.fruit: Poor set; no curd in cauliflower.
symptoms.wholePlant: N-hungry look on acid soils + whiptail leaves; legumes pale with few nodules.

howToFix.soilApplicationDose: 200-400 g/acre (tiny — usually with FYM or mixed for even spread)
howToFix.bestCropStage: Nursery/early growth; seed treatment for legumes/crucifers
howToFix.methodOfApplication: Seed treatment (best for legumes) or foliar; tiny doses
howToFix.precautions: Needed in TINY amounts — over-application is toxic to livestock (molybdenosis in grazing). Mix well for even spread.
Very low dose; higher Mo content than sodium molybdate.

howToFix.soilApplicationDose: Per lime requirement on acid soils
howToFix.methodOfApplication: Broadcast + incorporate — raising pH releases native soil Mo (often the real fix)
howToFix.precautions: Liming acid soils often cures Mo deficiency without adding Mo.

methodOfApplication.broadcast: Mo salts mixed with bulk (FYM/sand) for even spread of tiny doses; or lime to raise pH.
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: 0.05-0.1% Mo salt for quick correction, esp. cauliflower whiptail.
methodOfApplication.seedTreatment: BEST method for legumes/crucifers — coat seed with sodium/ammonium molybdate; tiny quantity, big effect on nodulation.

toxicity.whatHappens: Plant tolerates fairly high Mo, but excess Mo in FODDER causes MOLYBDENOSIS in grazing cattle (Cu deficiency in animals).
toxicity.plantToxicitySymptoms: Rarely visible in plants; concern is animal health from high-Mo fodder.
toxicity.correctionMethods: Avoid over-application; balance with copper in animal diet; don't over-lime + over-Mo together.

faq.q: Cauliflower me whiptail (patli strap patti, curd nahi) kya hai?
faq.a: Molybdenum ki kami (acid soil). Mitti me lime dein + 0.05-0.1% sodium molybdate foliar.

faq.q: Mo kis mitti me kam hota hai?
faq.a: ACID (kam pH) mitti me — baaki micros ke ulta. Lime se theek hota hai.

faq.q: Legume me pale + kam nodules — Mo?
faq.a: Haan — Mo nitrogenase (N-fixation) chalaता hai. Mo seed treatment + Rhizobium dein.
Bahut kam — gram me (200-400 g/acre). Zyada mat dein.

faq.q: Mo aur N deficiency me farak?
faq.a: Mo kami N-jaisi paleness deti hai PAR acid soil par + whiptail/distortion ke saath.
Legume/crucifer me seed treatment — chhoti maatra, bada asar.

faq.q: Lime se Mo theek hota hai?
faq.a: Haan — pH badhne se native Mo release hota hai; aksar bina Mo daale hi theek.
Plant ko kam, par high-Mo chaara pashuon me molybdenosis (Cu kami) karta hai.
